AccountUpdate.description:
Rename / re-describe / hide / move a real account (DESIGN §3.4).
``hidden`` toggles the display-only ``hidden_at`` timestamp; ``path``
moves the account and everything beneath it (decision 72).

``feed_start`` (§7.1, decision 40) is admin-only: explicit null clears,
absent leaves unchanged (model_fields_set distinguishes the two).
``feed_invert`` (§7.1, decision 43) is admin-only feed configuration
too; a plain bool, so absent/None simply leaves it unchanged.
``drift_basis_override`` (§7.3, decision 83) is admin-only as well, with
``feed_start``'s explicit-null-clears rule. ``holdings_source`` (§8,
decision 88) and ``feed_balance_is_cash`` (§7.3, decision 103) are
admin-only too; absent/None leaves them unchanged. ``min_balance`` (§3.4,
#466) is write scope, with the explicit-null-clears rule.

acquired_on.description: A hand-valued asset only: when it was acquired. An explicit null clears it; absent leaves it unchanged.
acquired_on.title: Acquired On

asset_description.description: A hand-valued asset only: an address, a VIN, a note (stored encrypted). An explicit null clears it; absent leaves it unchanged.
asset_description.title: Asset Description

asset_kind.description: A hand-valued asset (type property) only: what it is, a label and an icon. Absent leaves it unchanged. Write scope.
asset_kind.title: Asset Kind

balance_true_up.description: A brokerage account whose holdings come from the feed only (422 otherwise): after each sync, Purser compares the balance the broker reported with the account's cash plus the holdings from the same fetch and, when they differ by a cent or more, posts one labelled 'Balance adjustment' against Securities trade (equity.securities) for the difference, so a buy row the broker never sent cannot leave the account overstated. On by default; false stops future adjustments (past ones stay). Absent leaves it unchanged. Write scope.
balance_true_up.title: Balance True Up

drift_basis_override.description: Pin the ledger basis the post-sync balance-drift check compares this account's bank balance on: `posted_only` (the bank leaves pending charges out of its balance) or `pending_inclusive`. An explicit null clears the pin and the basis is learned from the account's sync history again; absent leaves it unchanged. Admin scope; checking, savings, cash and credit-card accounts only (422 otherwise).
drift_basis_override.title: Drift Basis Override

feed_balance_is_cash.description: Say that this brokerage account's feed balance is its CASH, as for a cash sweep whose positions are tracked by hand (`holdings_source` `manual`; 422 otherwise). The post-sync drift check then compares that balance with the account's transactions, like a checking account's. Off by default because many brokers report the whole account value instead. Turning it off clears a drift-basis pin; switching the account back to the feed turns it off. Admin scope.
feed_balance_is_cash.title: Feed Balance Is Cash

holdings_source.description: Where this brokerage account's holdings come from: `feed` (the SimpleFIN snapshots) or `manual` (positions recorded by hand, priced daily, and projected into the same snapshots). Switching to `manual` keeps every feed snapshot as history; the first manual snapshot is dated the day after the last feed one. Switching back to `feed` needs a feed mapping (422 without one) and changes no snapshot: the hand-tracked holdings stay in effect until the first sync after the switch, which ends them from its own date (a position the feed does not report ends there); positions stay, read-only. Admin scope; brokerage accounts only (422 otherwise).
holdings_source.title: Holdings Source

min_balance.description: The account's floor, in ledger sign: the nightly forecast scan emits `forecast.shortfall` when the 30-day projection drops below it (e.g. `500.00` to be warned before checking goes under $500; a credit card, negative when owed, takes a negative floor such as `-4500.00`). Checking, savings, cash and credit-card accounts only (422 otherwise); at most 4 decimal places. An explicit null clears the floor, and the account leaves the shortfall scan; absent leaves it unchanged. Write scope.
min_balance.title: Min Balance

path.description: Move the account to this ltree path, e.g. `liabilities.citicard`. Accounts beneath it move along and keep their relative paths. Refused with 409 when an account already sits at or under the new path, and with 422 for a malformed path or a destination under a category root such as `expenses`. Categories keep their paths.
path.title: Path

revalue_after_days.description: A hand-valued asset only: how many days its value may go without an update before Purser calls it stale (`asset.stale`, `whats_new`). An explicit null turns the reminder off; absent leaves it unchanged.
revalue_after_days.title: Revalue After Days

secured_by_id.description: A loan only: the hand-valued asset that secures it (a mortgage's house, a car loan's car); the asset then reports its equity. An explicit null clears it; absent leaves it unchanged. Write scope.
secured_by_id.title: Secured By Id

``skipped_scheduled`` counts Quicken reminder rows (not history, never
imported); ``skipped_investment`` counts QIF ``!Type:Invst`` records
(investment actions, never bank rows; decision 84); ``promoted`` counts
rows that posted an ``expected`` row an earlier import left, because the
file now marks them cleared (per leg for a transfer); ``uncleared`` is the
subset of the created rows that land ``expected`` because the file marks
them uncleared (decision 60). ``split_transfers`` (QIF ``S[Account]``
lines carved out of split rows as transfers) and ``split_remainders``
(split rows whose lines left part of the amount unexplained, booked to
the uncategorized placeholder) are sub-counts too (decision 87).

as_of.description: The date `quantity` holds (today or earlier; default today).
as_of.title: As Of

quantity.description: Shares held on `as_of`; records the opening `set_quantity` event. Omit to open the position empty and record its events separately.
quantity.title: Quantity

source_note.description: Where the figure came from, e.g. `broker holdings page, 2026-10-14`.
source_note.title: Source Note

symbol.description: The ticker, e.g. `ACME`; stored upper case. Letters, digits, `.` and `-` (share classes such as `BRK.B`).
symbol.title: Symbol

cash_in_lieu.description: `split` only: the cash the broker paid for the fractional share the split left. The fraction leaves in a `sell` recorded with the split (its proceeds are this amount) and reversed with it; `settle_on`, `transaction_id`, `force_cash`, `lot_method` and `lots` apply to that sale.
cash_in_lieu.title: Cash In Lieu

cost_basis.description: `set_quantity` only: the total basis after it. Omitted, a re-count of the count held just before keeps the basis, a changed count makes it unknown, and a count of 0 has a basis of 0.
cost_basis.title: Cost Basis

force_cash.description: Post the trade's cash even though the account already shows a row of exactly that amount around the settlement date (the 409 `cash_already_recorded` names it): for a true coincidence, a different payment that is not this trade's cash. The trade's audit row records the override and the row it posted over. Not with `transaction_id`, nor on a trade that moves no cash.
force_cash.title: Force Cash

funded_from.description: `buy` only. `cash`: the cost (quantity x price + fees, rounded half up to the cent) leaves the account's cash on the trade date (or `settle_on`). `none` (the default): the money came from outside the account, e.g. a payroll plan purchase.
funded_from.title: Funded From

gross_quantity.description: `vest` only: the gross units that vested (net `quantity` + withheld).
gross_quantity.title: Gross Quantity

kind.description: `set_quantity` (the absolute share count on that date), `buy` or `sell` (a change by `quantity`), `vest` (the NET shares an award vest delivered; `price` is the fair market value per share), `transfer_out` (shares that left with no price and no cash) or `split` (every share becomes `split_numerator` / `split_denominator` shares at the start of `occurred_on`, the effective date).
kind.title: Kind

lot.description: `buy`/`vest`: the lot it opens. A vest always opens one; a buy opens one when this is given or the position already tracks lots.

lot_method.description: `sell`/`transfer_out` on a position that tracks lots: draw on its lots first in, first out (`fifo`, by acquisition date), last in (`lifo`) or highest basis per share first (`hifo`; refused while a candidate lot has no basis). A method never takes unallocated shares. Give this or `lots`.
lot_method.title: Lot Method

lots.description: `sell`/`transfer_out`: specific identification. The quantities add up to `quantity`; each lot gives at most what it has left after every disposal recorded so far.
lots.title: Lots

occurred_on.description: Today or earlier; a future date is refused.
occurred_on.title: Occurred On

price.description: Per share, `buy`/`sell` only. A buy's price adds to the cost basis; without one the basis becomes unknown.
price.title: Price

proceeds_to.description: `sell` only. `cash` (the default): the net proceeds (quantity x price - fees, rounded half up to the cent) land on the account, balanced against the system account `equity.securities`, on the trade date (or `settle_on`). `none`: no cash moves, e.g. shares withheld for tax. Refused with 409 when the account already shows that cash.
proceeds_to.title: Proceeds To

quantity.description: Required for every kind but `split`, which takes a ratio instead.
quantity.title: Quantity

replaces.description: A reversed event of this position, on the same date, that this one corrects. The correction takes that event's place in the day's order; without `replaces` a new event goes after every event already recorded that day.
replaces.title: Replaces

settle_on.description: When the cash posts: by default the trade date, the day the shares leave the holdings (so net worth does not dip); a later date posts it at settlement instead. The double-count check looks from the trade to five days after `settle_on`, or after the next business day (T+1) when it is not given. A trade that links its cash (`transaction_id`) settles on that row's date, and its window comes from the trade alone (next business day + 5 days).
settle_on.title: Settle On

split_denominator.description: `split` only: the old shares that become `split_numerator` new ones.
split_denominator.title: Split Denominator

split_numerator.description: `split` only: new shares for every `split_denominator` old ones (2 for a 2:1 forward split, 1 for a 1:10 reverse split).
split_numerator.title: Split Numerator

transaction_id.description: Link the trade's cash to this posted row on the account (one real leg, one category leg) instead of posting new cash: the row is re-booked to `equity.securities` through the reversal-pair correction. info.description:
Purser is a privately hosted finance back-end for your personal AI agent.
It is mostly headless: use the MCP endpoint at `/mcp` or these REST endpoints
with a Bearer token. The web UI provides administrative controls.
Purser stores records and performs calculations; your agent supplies the AI.

Conventions: amounts are decimal strings (negative = money out); accounts and
categories accept a UUID or an ltree path; posted transactions are immutable
(edits become linked reversal pairs); writes need the `write` scope and are
audited and reversible. Aggregate questions (spending, net worth,
forecasts) have dedicated endpoints — never sum transaction rows client-side.

post.description:
Record a `set_quantity`, `buy`, `sell`, `vest`, `transfer_out` or
`split`.

A `split` takes `split_numerator` and `split_denominator` (2 and 1 for a
2:1 forward split, 1 and 10 for a 1:10 reverse one): at the start of
`occurred_on` every share held the day before becomes that ratio of
shares (six places), each lot keeping its total basis, acquisition date
and term. With `cash_in_lieu`, the fractional share left leaves in a
`sell` whose proceeds are that amount (`cash_in_lieu` in the answer),
reversed with the split. Reversing the split restores the shares, the
lots and the cash exactly.

On a position that tracks lots, a `sell` or `transfer_out` names the
lots it draws on (`lot_method` or `lots`; 422 `allocation_required`
otherwise), a `buy` opens a lot unless `unallocated`, and every write is
refused (422 with `detail.code`) that would leave a lot below zero or
the lots holding more than the position on any day. The whole history is checked
after it: an event that would leave the position below zero on ANY date
(a backdated sell, say) is refused with 422 naming that date. Any event,
a backdate or not, that would leave this position holding shares on a
day a CLOSED position in the same symbol held them or sold out is
refused with 409 (positions never overlap).

A sale moves its net proceeds to the account's cash unless `proceeds_to`
is `none`; a buy takes its cost from the cash only with `funded_from`
`cash`. That cash is one posted system row against `equity.securities`
(it joins the unreviewed set), or an existing row linked with
`transaction_id`. When the account already shows a posted one-sided row
of exactly that amount around the settlement date, the call is refused
with 409 naming it, so the cash is never counted twice: link that row,
